subject: Insurely privacy check: DPA path, SCC module choice, controller/processor confirmation
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Costa <elena.costa@insurely.com>, Gabe Turner <gabe.turner@insurely.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & asks — DPA / SCC module / SOC 2

Hi Elena & Gabe,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on how Insurely plans to use Redwood for claims automation and underwriting enrichment. Quick recap and the three items we need to move contracting forward: 

1) Controller vs. Processor: you mentioned Insurely will be the controller for personal data in the workflows we discussed, with Redwood acting as a processor when we host inference. Please confirm that alignment (one-line reply is fine).

2) SCC module preference: you expressed a leaning toward SCC Module II (data controller to processor) but wanted to confirm. If Module II is acceptable we’ll route the DPA that way. If you prefer Module III/IV, let us know so legal can adjust.

3) Security evidence: please share the following when available — SOC 2 Type II report (redacted OK), and if you prefer we’ll send our standard Vendor Security Questionnaire (VSQ) for you to fill; alternatively, we can accept a completed VSQ you already maintain.

Next steps I’ll take: attach a blank VSQ template (for quick turnaround) and a first-pass DPA drafted for Module II. Ben from Legal is cc’d and will weigh in on any retention/HIPAA-specific language. Can you confirm the controller designation and SCC preference by EOD Tuesday 10/26?

Attachments: Insurely_VSQ_20271022.pdf (blank questionnaire), DPA_Draft_Insurely_20271022.docx (first-pass)

Thanks,
Priya

Thanks Priya — quick responses inline: 

> Controller vs. Processor: you mentioned Insurely will be the controller...
Yes — Insurely will be the controller for customer PII in the use cases discussed. Redwood will act as a processor for hosted inference.

> SCC module preference: you expressed a leaning toward SCC Module II...
We agree with Module II (controller -> processor). Our procurement team prefers the more prescriptive Module II for EU cross-border flows.

> Security evidence: please share SOC 2 Type II...
We can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II report by the end of next week (estimate 10/29). In the meantime, we attached a completed VSQ with some high-level answers for the controls that apply to our environment. We left items related to third-party inference providers for you to confirm.

Ben — looping you in to note Insurely confirms controller role and Module II preference. Can Legal review the attached DPA draft and flag any retention/HIPAA language we should tighten? Specifically:
- Retention period for derived model artifacts and logs (Insurely asked about 18 months vs 36 months)
- Any required business associate agreement (BAA) language if HIPAA applies (Insurely indicated some downstream customers may be in healthcare)

Ben, happy to schedule a 30-min legal-ops sync if that helps; otherwise, a redline to the DPA would be great.

Elena/Gabe — next practical steps from our side:
- I’ll provide a DocuSign flow for the DPA once legal signs off.
- Redwood will prepare a short SOC 2 evidence package summary to share with your procurement team before the full report arrives.

Thanks — Priya

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & asks — DPA / SCC module / SOC 2

Priya / Laura — I reviewed the DPA draft. High level notes: 

- Module: Module II is fine for controller->processor flows; it matches the stated relationship.
- Retention: Recommend we propose 24 months default (compromise between 18/36) and include a customer-specific retention override in Section 4.2. That keeps flexibility and addresses Insurely's ask.
- HIPAA / BAA: We should include a clause that says Redwood will enter into a standalone BAA where the customer designates PHI in scope — avoid baking HIPAA language directly into the DPA to keep it clean.
- Logs & model artifacts: limit retention of inference logs to 30 days by default; offer an opt-in extended logs retention addendum for analytics customers.

I’ll attach a redlined DPA and a short note for Priya to send to Insurely.

Attachment: DPA_Draft_Insurely_20271022_redline.docx

Ben
Director, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Hi Priya / Ben,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the redline, Ben — that approach sounds reasonable. Confirming:
- Insurely = Controller; Redwood = Processor.
- SCC Module II is acceptable.
- We accept the proposed 24-month default retention with the ability to request a different term during contracting.
- For HIPAA: we will flag PHI use cases during contracting; a separate BAA is fine.

We reviewed Ben’s redline and have two small asks (non-substantive):
1) Add a straightforward contact point for security evidence requests (we prefer a named contact + email).
2) Clarify that Redwood’s inference cache may be subject to the retention term — we want explicit confirmation for cache purge timing.

We’ll provide the full SOC 2 Type II redacted report next Friday (10/29). In the meantime we can sign the DPA after you update contact points and the cache sentence. Please send the updated DPA via DocuSign; we should have sign-off from procurement and legal within 3 business days of receiving the updated doc.
